why: Critical bugs: firstName returns the second word instead of first, breaking welcomeBack. Fix index [1] to [0] and add edge case handling.

findings.title: `firstName` returns the second word, not the first
findings.body: `firstName(name)` returns the second word, not the first. `split(" ")[1]` accesses index 1 (second element), but should use index 0 for first name. For "Ada Lovelace", it returns "Lovelace" instead of "Ada".
findings.verified: Confirmed by running: firstName('Ada Lovelace') returns 'Lovelace'

findings.title: `welcomeBack` greets users with wrong name
findings.body: `welcomeBack(name)` is broken because it depends on `firstName()`. It will say "Welcome back, Lovelace!" instead of "Welcome back, Ada!".
findings.verified: Confirmed by running: welcomeBack('Ada Lovelace') returns 'Welcome back, Lovelace!'

findings.title: No handling for edge cases
findings.body: No handling for edge cases: single name ("Ada") returns undefined, empty string returns undefined. Should handle these gracefully.

findings.title: Test assertion too loose to catch the bug
findings.body: Test uses toMatch with only prefix pattern `/^Welcome back, /`, doesn't verify the actual first name. Would pass with buggy "Lovelace" output.
findings.verified: Confirmed: regex matches both correct and buggy output
